title: Lixity — Read Your Manuscript, Compare Prose, Trace Research
description: Revise your manuscript with evidence from the text. Compare chapters and drafts, build character dossiers, and connect source quotations. Analysis runs locally.
headline:
Revise your manuscript.
Keep the research in reach.
intro: See why a passage was flagged, compare a revision, and keep characters and sources beside your text. Lixity works on your computer with your Markdown or plain-text manuscript.
demo_note: Fictional English manuscript. Interactive read-only demo. No account or upload required.
preview: The real workspace: read your prose undisturbed, then reveal rhythm, dialogue, and scene patterns whenever you choose.
tasks_title: From a marked passage to the next revision
read_text: Keep your review marks by the text as you write with local autosave. Compare the draft with the saved manuscript under the same analysis settings before applying it.
research_title: Follow a character through the manuscript
research_text: Draft a dossier from the prose and review its chapter distribution and passages in context. Keep your notes, claims, and exact source quotations beside the text.
share_text: In the development build, download the selected dossier version as an A4 PDF with its saved notes, tables, excerpts, and source quotations. For the manuscript, choose a print layout or prepare a reading website with chapter limits and spoiler controls.
principle: Inspect the signal. Make your own decision.
principle_text: Measurements describe patterns in the supplied text. They do not grade literary quality or tell you how to rewrite a passage. Inspect the counted words and sentences, read them in context, and decide whether a difference matters.
start_text: Install Lixity locally on Windows, macOS, or Linux. Open any Markdown or plain-text draft by following the setup guide.
scope: This command installs the package published on PyPI. The demo and source documentation describe development version v{version}.
languages_text: The site and app interface are available in seven languages. Choose the manuscript analysis language explicitly; technical documentation remains in English.
limits: Language rules and coverage vary by language, with German and English offering the deepest checks. Switching the interface language never alters your manuscript.
feedback_text: Tell us what you were writing, checking, or sharing, and where the studio helped or got in your way. You never need to send your manuscript.
linguistics_title: See why the text was marked
linguistics_text: Open a note about sentence rhythm, quotations, or repeated words and inspect the counted text. Compare chapters and follow available evidence back to the prose to decide what deserves a closer read.
language_suggestion: Prefer another language? Use your saved choice or a language supported by your browser.
tour_note: Silent recording of the fictional Warehouse 4 project in the development build.
tour_read: Open a review suggestion and jump to its passage.
tour_passage: See which words counted, why the sentence was marked, and what to check.
tour_compare: Compare the unsaved draft with the manuscript under the same settings.
tour_chapters: Open a chapter measurement and see which chapter it describes.
tour_dossier: Open Mara’s dossier and read her appearances in context.
tour_pdf: Download the saved dossier version as a PDF.
tour_error: The video could not load. Explore the interactive demo instead.
workflow: Read, write, and check what changes in the text. Built-in analysis runs offline. Optional speech, map services, and connected AI clients have their own network and data-handling requirements.
compare_lead: Use Lixity to compare prose patterns, inspect the counted text, and trace research links while you read. It complements writing and planning tools; its measurements support your review and do not replace an editor.
compare_lix_privacy: Manuscripts and built-in analysis stay local and offline; optional online tools only on click
compare_cld_privacy: Cloud processing with an account and internet connection
compare_pln_privacy: Local or cloud storage depending on the app (e.g. Plottr desktop, Fictionary online)
compare_lix_method: Sentence rhythm, dialogue share, and word echoes by chapter, linked to exact passages
compare_cld_method: Rule & AI suggestions, readability scores, optional rewrites
compare_pln_method: Scene checklists & story arcs, little sentence- or word-level feedback
compare_lix_research: Local archive for text, PDFs, images and video. Link sources to passages and compare drafts.
compare_pln_research: Character & plot notes without linked original sources
compare_lix_license: Free, open source (AGPL-3.0), no subscription, 7 languages
compare_col_oss: OSS novel tools (e.g. novelWriter, Manuskript, bibisco)
compare_dsk_privacy: Local storage & offline writing; occasional vendor license checks
compare_oss_privacy: 100% local & offline (plain text, Markdown, or local database), no cloud lock-in
compare_dsk_method: Style & filler checks (Papyrus Autor) or binder & compile workflow (Scrivener)
compare_oss_method: Outlining, corkboards & character sheets; no statistical prose analysis
compare_dsk_research: Research folders & corkboards, without direct source links tied to draft history
compare_oss_research: Project notes, tags & plot trees, without a source archive or draft-level metrics
compare_dsk_license: Paid licenses. Scrivener licenses are platform-specific. Major upgrades may carry a fee.
compare_oss_license: Open source (GPL-3.0), free core app (bibisco offers paid extras)
compare_lix_dossiers: Character and scene drafts extracted from prose; linked dossiers, collections, timelines, and maps
compare_dsk_dossiers: Character database, mind map & corkboard; maintained manually
compare_oss_dossiers: Character sheets, tags & corkboard; maintained manually
compare_pln_dossiers: Timelines, scene cards, and character arcs; planning only, without prose analysis
